name: WOKI
tagline: Ask for help and coordinate rescues without internet, with remote visibility once the network returns.
problem: When an earthquake takes down the cell network, asking for help stops being an interface problem and becomes a communication and coordination problem.
solution: A person joins the Wi-Fi of a TTGO LoRa node without installing an app, reports what they need with GPS or a description; the node sends a short LoRa (915 MHz) packet, waits for an acknowledgement and retries. A Raspberry Pi command center stores incidents in SQLite, prioritizes them, recommends compatible resources and lets an operator authorize dispatch; the resource accepts and reports progress until the incident closes. An online replica (Vercel + Supabase) syncs pending events when internet returns but never executes critical actions.
demo_moment: Not described publicly. The write-up lists LoRa messaging with acknowledgements between boards on real hardware, an offline dashboard, and an automatically verified flow from SOS through triage, dispatch, acceptance and resolution.

why_it_stood_out.claim: Zero-install entry: a phone joins the node's Wi-Fi to report an emergency; delivery uses acknowledgements and retries over LoRa.
Offline is the operational source of truth; the cloud hub only mirrors and syncs when the network returns, so a cloud failure never stops operations.
Shipped beyond a slide: a public hub, an isolated demo command center, printable enclosures and a LoRa flow visualization.
Entered the joint most crowded Bogotá track (7 of 24 submissions in Emergencies) with physical hardware and a one-line promise — works when the internet does not.

lessons: State the failure condition the product survives (no internet) in the tagline; judges remember constraints.
Separate the operational path (local, authoritative) from the showcase path (cloud mirror) so the demo cannot be broken by venue Wi-Fi.

sources.note: Team-written project page hosted by the organizer; no placement.
